Atzori 2011 (PMID 21810918, epub 2011-08-02) abstract quote verbatim; iv dalotuzumab in advanced solid tumours, so drug, route iv and other_disease fit. Direct readout; same holds.

entries.note: Weickhardt 2012 (PMID 22237261) quote verbatim: cixutumumab iv with full-dose erlotinib, unselected NSCLC. Drug, route, combination_with fit; xenografts used h7C10, product_in_model false; Goetsch states no exposure or margin.
Goetsch 2005 abstract quote verbatim (A549, h7C10 plus vinorelbine or antibody 225). Drug dalotuzumab, route iv, opener of the A549 dalotuzumab track: correct.

entries.note: Ramalingam 2011 (PMID 22025157, epub 2011-10-24) quote verbatim; primary 12-week PFS rate null; R1507 iv plus erlotinib vs placebo plus erlotinib, design in note; NCT00760929 results 2021-01-05. Contra holds.

entries.note: Novello 2017 (PMID 27464970) quote verbatim; cixutumumab iv plus pemetrexed/cisplatin, stage IV nonsquamous; product_in_model false. Goetsch abstract makes no tolerability claim, so untested no_prediction holds.

Gong 2009 (PMID 19806209) abstract quote verbatim; R1507 = teprotumumab, iv in patients compared; biomarker_selected fits a total-IGF-1R prediction. Note's 'Habben could not be read' is stale; status unaffected.

FDA PharmR BLA 761143 (bundle txt line 3635) gives the 7-week iv cynomolgus study title for Ro 485-8696 (R1507 = teprotumumab), initiated 2004-11-03. Drug teprotumumab, route iv; opener untested 2004 holds.

entries.note: Habben 2011 ASCO 7584 sentence seen via search text (abstract body not opened): IGF1R-level subgroups showed no impact on 12-week PFS in NO21160, R1507 iv plus erlotinib. Fields fit; prospective after Gong 2009: contra.

entries.note: Moran 2014 quote verbatim; phase II primary endpoint PFS (2.5 vs 1.6 mo, ns); drug, iv, erlotinib, product_in_model true fit. Full text: presented at IASLC 14th WCLC, July 2011, so year 2011.
entries.adjudication_note: Status contra agreed. Rule 6: Moran 2014 full text says results presented at IASLC 14th WCLC, July 2011; the congress date is earliest public, so year 2011, not 2014. AACR 2009 mention predates phase II results.

missing: safety: contra entry, model = cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology of R1507/teprotumumab (Roche reports Jul-Aug 2005, up to 39 weeks; product_in_model true), source FDA BLA 761143 Pharmacology/Toxicology review (http://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2021/761143Orig1s000PharmR.pdf, tier 2, comparison_stated true). Quote (11.4): 'the monkey model predicted the clinical reduced weight gain/weight loss and decreased serum ALP, but not the clinical infusion reactions, exacerbation of inflammatory bowel disease, or hyperglycemia.' Executive summary: 'The monkey toxicology studies did not predict these effects.' Patient harm is in TED patients, so imported_from the thyroid eye disease MONDO id; hyperglycemia is on-target (IGF1R/IR) and also seen with cixutumumab in NSCLC (Novello 2017 9.4% vs 1.2%; E3508). Year = review posting (approval Jan 2020; file under nda/2021). Monkeys can show hyperglycemia, so this is a scored miss, not silence a species could not show.

efficacy (candidate competing model): Gong et al. 2009 PLoS One, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0007273 (PMID 19806209), a member-drug (R1507) NSCLC model: in 22 NSCLC lines only 5 were moderately sensitive, linked to high total IGF-1R, i.e. it predicted little benefit in unselected NSCLC. Published Oct 2009, before the Ramalingam result (Oct 2011). Not the model the draft scored; recorded so the adjudicator can decide whether it, not A549/h7C10, is the 'best model' for the R1507 trial.

No press release, SEC filing or EMA document found reporting an additional member-drug NSCLC failure; figitumumab's NSCLC phase 3 failures are outside the member list (figitumumab is not a member) and correctly absent.

efficacy (parallel track r1507-nsclc-cell-line-panel): likely 2011 contra, patient side Habben et al. J Clin Oncol 29:15_suppl 7584 (doi:10.1200/jco.2011.29.15_suppl.7584, NO21160 R1507+erlotinib): search-engine text of the abstract reads 'No significant impact on treatment was observed when the PFS rates of patient subgroups defined by other biomarkers, including IGF1R level, were compared'; abstract body 403 on ascopubs and absent from Europe PMC/Crossref, so it needs a verbatim read before entry.
rule_questions: Efficacy pairing across partner drugs: the A549 model tested h7C10 + vinorelbine or + anti-EGFR antibody 225; the trials ran R1507 + erlotinib (TKI), cixutumumab + pemetrexed/cisplatin and + carboplatin/paclitaxel/bevacizumab. Does 'conditions the model never tested' cover a different combination partner of the same mechanism (EGFR blockade, cytotoxic chemo), or only population/biomarker conditions? Ramalingam attributes the failure to lack of a predictive biomarker, which the unselected A549 model also lacked, so I kept contra.

Opening (untested) entries at model_first_use_year: may they cite a later patient-side source (dose and safety cells cite 2012 and 2016 papers in 2005 entries), or must the opening entry cite the model source dated to that year?

When two prospective models of member drugs disagree before the trial (h7C10/A549 predicting near-complete inhibition; R1507 22-line panel predicting low unselected sensitivity), which is 'the best model in the context' for scoring the R1507 trial?

Safety contra whose patient harm is documented for the same drug only in another indication (TED) while NSCLC trials of a different member (cixutumumab) show the same on-target harm: imported_from the TED id, or a direct NSCLC comparison via the pooled on-target rule?
